question: The focal length of a concave mirror is 24 cm. Following New Cartesian Sign Convention, its centre of curvature is located at:
solution:
The correct answer is __**-48 cm**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The focal length of a concave mirror is given as 24 cm, following the New Cartesian Sign Convention.
 
• According to the sign convention, the focal length (f) of a concave mirror is negative, so **f = -24 cm**.
 
• The centre of curvature (C) of a concave mirror is located at a distance equal to twice the focal length from the pole of the mirror.
 
• Thus, the distance to the centre of curvature is **2f = 2(-24 cm) = -48 cm**.
 
• Therefore, the centre of curvature is located at -48 cm.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **New Cartesian Sign Convention** is used to determine the signs of the distances measured along the principal axis of the mirror.
 
• Distances measured in the direction of the incident light (towards the mirror) are considered negative.
 
• Distances measured against the direction of the incident light (away from the mirror) are considered positive.
 
• **The focal length of concave mirrors is always negative, while that of convex mirrors is positive.**
